    *   The number of vertices in the Steiner Tree is $S$. The cost is $S - n$.
    *   We want to find the maximum possible value of this cost over all sets of $n$ black cells.

    *   If we place $n$ points in a grid, the minimum spanning tree (MST) length is roughly $n \cdot \text{average distance}$.
    *   If we place points in a $\sqrt{n} \times \sqrt{n}$ grid with spacing $\sqrt{n}$, the distance between adjacent points is $\sqrt{n}$.
    *   Total length $\approx (n-1) \sqrt{n} \approx n^{3/2}$.
    *   The cost is $n^{3/2} - n$.
    *   So $f(n)$ should grow as $n^{3/2}$.
